## Setup

```{r libraries}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
```

---

## Figure A — EAC Pathway and SST Gradient

This figure uses a schematic SST gradient based on published climatological
values from Iha et al. (2023) and Butler et al. (2020), avoiding the need
for large data downloads.

```{r eac-data}
# Schematic SST grid based on published climatological means
# Northern sites ~15.5°C, southern sites ~14°C (Iha et al. 2023, Table 1)
# Gradient represents EAC influence pushing warm water south

sst_grid <- expand.grid(
  lon = seq(138, 158, by = 0.5),
  lat = seq(-45, -20, by = 0.5)
)

# SST decreases from north to south and from east (EAC) to west
sst_grid$sst <- with(sst_grid,
  26 +
  (lat + 20) * 0.35 +           # cooler toward south
  (lon - 155) * 0.25 +          # cooler away from EAC
  ifelse(lon > 149 & lat > -40, # EAC warm tongue
         (lon - 149) * 0.4, 0)
)

# Clip to realistic range
sst_grid$sst <- pmin(pmax(sst_grid$sst, 12), 28)

# Mask land approximately
sst_grid <- sst_grid %>%
  filter(!(lon > 144 & lon < 149 & lat > -44 & lat < -40)) %>%  # Tasmania
  filter(!(lon > 140 & lon < 150 & lat > -39 & lat < -34))       # VIC mainland

# EAC pathway schematic
eac_main <- data.frame(
  lon = c(153.5, 153.0, 152.5, 152.0, 151.5, 151.0, 150.5, 150.5, 150.8, 151.0),
  lat = c(-22.0, -24.0, -26.0, -28.0, -30.0, -32.0, -34.0, -36.0, -38.0, -40.0)
)

eac_extension <- data.frame(
  lon = c(150.5, 150.0, 149.5, 149.0, 148.5, 148.0, 147.5),
  lat = c(-34.0, -36.0, -38.0, -40.0, -41.0, -42.0, -43.5)
)

eac_separation <- data.frame(
  lon = c(150.5, 152.0, 154.0, 156.0),
  lat = c(-34.0, -34.5, -35.0, -36.0)
)

aus_states <- ne_countries(country = "Australia",
                           scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
```

```{r sst-map, fig.width=6, fig.height=8, fig.cap="**Figure 3A.** Schematic sea surface temperature (SST) gradient along the east Australian coast, illustrating the influence of the East Australian Current (EAC). White arrows show the approximate EAC pathway, with the dashed extension indicating warm, nutrient-poor water being transported southward toward Tasmania. SST values are based on published climatological means (Butler et al., 2020; Iha et al., 2023). EAC pathway schematic based on Suthers et al. (2011) and Holbrook & Bindoff (1997)."}

p_sst <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(
    data = sst_grid,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = sst),
    interpolate = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours  = c("#053061", "#2166ac", "#4393c3", "#92c5de",
                 "#fddbc7", "#f4a582", "#d6604d", "#b2182b", "#67001f"),
    name     = "SST (°C)",
    na.value = "white",
    limits   = c(12, 28),
    breaks   = seq(12, 28, 4)
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = aus_states, fill = "#d4c5a9", colour = "#8a7560",
          linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_path(
    data  = eac_main,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat),
    colour = "white", linewidth = 1.2, lineend = "round", linejoin = "round",
    arrow  = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm"), type = "closed", ends = "last")
  ) +
  geom_path(
    data  = eac_extension,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat),
    colour = "white", linewidth = 0.9, linetype = "dashed", lineend = "round",
    arrow  = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), type = "closed", ends = "last")
  ) +
  geom_path(
    data  = eac_separation,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat),
    colour = "white", linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dotted", lineend = "round"
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 154.5, y = -25,
           label = "East Australian\nCurrent (EAC)",
           colour = "white", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold",
           lineheight = 0.85, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 151.5, y = -39.5,
           label = "EAC Extension\n(warm, nutrient-poor)",
           colour = "white", size = 2.6, fontface = "italic",
           lineheight = 0.85, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 145.0, y = -42.3,
           label = "Tasmania", colour = "#5a4a30", size = 3.5,
           fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 142.5, y = -37.5,
           label = "Victoria", colour = "#5a4a30", size = 3.0,
           fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 139.5, y = -34.0,
           label = "South\nAustralia", colour = "#5a4a30", size = 2.8,
           fontface = "italic", lineheight = 0.85) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(138, 158), ylim = c(-45, -20), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(140, 158, 4),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "\u00b0E")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-44, -20, 4),
                     labels = function(y) paste0(abs(y), "\u00b0S")) +
  labs(
    title   = "A) Sea surface temperature and East Australian Current",
    x       = "Longitude",
    y       = "Latitude",
    caption = "Schematic SST gradient based on Butler et al. (2020) and Iha et al. (2023).\nEAC pathway based on Suthers et al. (2011) and Holbrook & Bindoff (1997)."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, colour = "#1a3a4a"),
    plot.caption      = element_text(size = 7, colour = "#888888", hjust = 0),
    panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "#cde8f0", colour = NA),
    panel.grid        = element_line(colour = "#b0cfd8", linewidth = 0.2),
    plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    legend.position   = "right",
    legend.key.height = unit(1.2, "cm"),
    plot.margin       = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

p_sst
```

## Figure B — North-south SST and Nutrient Gradient

Climatological SST values per region from published literature (Iha et al., 2023;
Butler et al., 2020). Nutrient values are indicative based on published
descriptions of EAC nutrient dynamics (Suthers et al., 2011; Kämpf, 2015).

```{r transect-data}
# Published mean SST values per region (Iha et al. 2023, Table 1)
# North TAS sites A-C: 15.4-15.5°C mean annual SST
# South TAS sites D-F: 14.0-14.1°C mean annual SST
# VIC/Wilderness Coast: ~17-18°C (warmer, EAC influenced)

transect <- data.frame(
  lat     = c(-37.5, -38.5, -40.0, -41.0, -41.5, -42.0, -43.0, -43.5, -44.0),
  region  = c("Wilderness\nCoast (VIC)", "Wilderness\nCoast (VIC)",
              "North TAS", "North TAS",
              "Northeast TAS", "Northeast TAS",
              "Southeast TAS", "Southeast TAS", "Southeast TAS"),
  sst     = c(17.8, 17.2, 15.5, 15.4, 15.0, 14.5, 14.1, 14.0, 13.8),
  # Indicative nitrate values (umol/L) based on EAC nutrient dynamics
  # Higher in southern/upwelling regions, lower under EAC influence
  nitrate = c(1.2, 1.5, 1.8, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 3.8, 4.2)
)

region_colours <- c(
  "Wilderness\nCoast (VIC)" = "#c0392b",
  "North TAS"               = "#8b2fc9",
  "Northeast TAS"           = "#e07b39",
  "Southeast TAS"           = "#2e8b57"
)
```

```{r sst-transect, fig.width=8, fig.height=4, fig.cap="**Figure 3B.** North-south gradient in mean annual sea surface temperature (SST) from the Wilderness Coast (Victoria) to Southeast Tasmania. Points represent published climatological mean SST values per region. The temperature gradient reflects the southward penetration of warm EAC water, with North Tasmanian sites consistently warmer than Southeast Tasmanian sites. Values from Iha et al. (2023) and Butler et al. (2020)."}

p_sst_transect <- ggplot(transect, aes(x = lat, y = sst, colour = region)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-38.2, -40.5, -42.5),
             colour = "grey80", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = -37.8, y = 13.9, label = "VIC",
           size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = -40.0, y = 13.9, label = "N TAS",
           size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = -41.8, y = 13.9, label = "NE TAS",
           size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = -43.5, y = 13.9, label = "SE TAS",
           size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 18, linetype = "dotted",
             colour = "#b2182b", linewidth = 0.6) +
  annotate("text", x = -44.5, y = 18.2,
           label = "~18\u00b0C thermal\ntolerance threshold",
           size = 2.4, colour = "#b2182b", hjust = 1, lineheight = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = region_colours, name = "Region") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(-38, -40, -41.5, -43.5),
    labels = function(x) paste0(abs(x), "\u00b0S"),
    name   = "Latitude"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name   = "Mean annual SST (\u00b0C)",
    limits = c(13.5, 19)
  ) +
  labs(
    title   = "B) North\u2013south SST gradient",
    caption = "Published climatological SST means from Iha et al. (2023) and Butler et al. (2020).\nDotted line indicates approximate thermal tolerance threshold for giant kelp."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, colour = "#1a3a4a"),
    plot.caption     = element_text(size = 7, colour = "#888888", hjust = 0),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    legend.position  = "right",
    plot.margin      = margin(5, 10, 5, 5)
  )

p_sst_transect
```

```{r nutrient-transect, fig.width=8, fig.height=4, fig.cap="**Figure 3C.** North-south gradient in surface nitrate concentration from the Wilderness Coast (Victoria) to Southeast Tasmania. Nitrate concentrations are lowest in northern sites under direct EAC influence, increasing toward southern Tasmania where cooler, nutrient-rich water historically upwelled through Bass Strait. Values are indicative based on published descriptions of EAC nutrient dynamics (Suthers et al., 2011; Kämpf, 2015; Fernández et al., 2023)."}

p_nutrient_transect <- ggplot(transect, aes(x = lat, y = nitrate,
                                             colour = region)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-38.2, -40.5, -42.5),
             colour = "grey80", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_area(aes(group = 1), fill = "#92c5de", alpha = 0.25,
            colour = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  annotate("text", x = -37.8, y = 0.3, label = "VIC",
           size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = -40.0, y = 0.3, label = "N TAS",
           size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = -41.8, y = 0.3, label = "NE TAS",
           size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = -43.5, y = 0.3, label = "SE TAS",
           size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", fontface = "italic") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = region_colours, name = "Region") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(-38, -40, -41.5, -43.5),
    labels = function(x) paste0(abs(x), "\u00b0S"),
    name   = "Latitude"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name   = "Surface nitrate (\u03bcmol/L)",
    limits = c(0, 5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title   = "C) North\u2013south surface nitrate gradient",
    caption = "Indicative values based on Suthers et al. (2011), Kämpf (2015) and Fernández et al. (2023).\nLow nitrate in northern sites reflects nutrient-poor EAC influence."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, colour = "#1a3a4a"),
    plot.caption     = element_text(size = 7, colour = "#888888", hjust = 0),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    legend.position  = "right",
    plot.margin      = margin(5, 10, 5, 5)
  )

p_nutrient_transect
```

## Save outputs

```{r save, eval=FALSE}
ggsave("kelp_EAC_SST_map.png",
       plot = p_sst, width = 6, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

ggsave("kelp_SST_transect.png",
       plot = p_sst_transect, width = 8, height = 4, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

ggsave("kelp_nutrient_transect.png",
       plot = p_nutrient_transect, width = 8, height = 4, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

## References

Butler, C.L. et al. (2020). Multi-decadal decline in cover of giant kelp
*Macrocystis pyrifera* at the southern limit of its Australian range.
*Marine Ecology Progress Series*, 653, 1–18.

Holbrook, N.J. & Bindoff, N.L. (1997). Interannual and decadal temperature
variability in the southwest Pacific Ocean. *Journal of Climate*, 10, 1035–1049.

Iha, C. et al. (2023). Population genomic analysis reveals genetic structure
and thermal-tolerant genotypes in remnant Tasmanian giant kelp populations.
*bioRxiv*.

Kämpf, J. (2015). Phytoplankton blooms on the western shelf of Tasmania.
*Ocean Science*, 11, 1–11.

Suthers, I.M. et al. (2011). The strengthening East Australian Current, its
eddies and biological effects. *Deep Sea Research Part II*, 58, 538–546.

Fernández, P.A. et al. (2023). The influence of ammonium to nitrate ratio
on the thermal responses of early life stages of giant kelp.
*Algal Research*, 72, 103114.
